key_insight: The paper gives the first finite-time convergence guarantees for exact Natural Policy Gradient in finite-horizon MDPs, showing sublinear convergence with constant step size and geometric convergence with increasing step sizes.
engineering_relevance: This provides practical guidance for selecting NPG step-size schedules in reinforcement-learning systems such as TRPO/PPO-style optimization, especially when horizon length is known.
method: Analyze exact NPG in finite-horizon MDPs with known, horizon-dependent transition kernels.
Prove an O(H^2/t) convergence rate for constant step size and extend it to linear MDPs under a full-support population-projection oracle.
Establish linear convergence with a problem-dependent geometric rate under increasing step sizes, including a robust horizon-based schedule.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical finite-time convergence analysis and explicit rates from the derived proofs, rather than empirical experiments.
watch_item: The strongest guarantees rely on exact dynamics/known kernels and, for the linear-MDP extension, an exact population-projection oracle with full-support assumptions, which may be difficult to realize in practice.
paper_title: Finite-Time Analysis of the Natural Policy Gradient in Finite-Horizon Markov Decision Processes
